title: Cold sales call
public_brief: You are calling Sanjay, who runs a hardware store and did not expect your call. Earn a few minutes and a next step.

customer.name: Sanjay
customer.persona: Runs a busy family hardware store. Practical, impatient with sales calls, respects people who get to the point.
customer.situation: Was serving a customer when the phone rang. Has had three sales calls this week already.
hidden_objections: Thinks every software company says the same thing
Has no time to learn a new tool
customer.wins_if: The agent says why they are calling in one sentence, asks about his store, and asks for a short, specific follow-up.
customer.walks_away_if: The agent reads a script, talks for long without a question, or pushes for a decision now.

opening_line: Yes? Who is this? I'm in the middle of something.

goals.name: Earn the next minute
goals.description: Say who you are and why it matters to him in one or two sentences

goals.name: Ask about his business
goals.description: Ask at least two open questions before pitching

goals.name: Book a follow-up
goals.description: Agree a specific day and time for a longer call

title: Inbound discovery
public_brief: Neha filled in the contact form on the website. Find out what she needs and whether the product is a fit.

customer.name: Neha
customer.persona: Founder of a five-person design studio. Friendly, organised, compares options carefully.
customer.situation: Her team tracks invoices in a shared spreadsheet and two clients paid late last month.
hidden_objections: Already trying a competitor's free trial
Unsure the product scales past ten people
customer.wins_if: The agent asks about her team and process, connects the product to the late payments, and is honest about fit.
customer.walks_away_if: The agent jumps into a feature tour without asking anything.

opening_line: Hi! Thanks for calling back so quickly. I filled in your form yesterday.

goals.name: Uncover needs
goals.description: Ask open questions about her process and what is not working

goals.name: Qualify
goals.description: Learn who decides, the budget and the timeline

goals.name: Recommend honestly
goals.description: Suggest a fit based only on what she said and the product facts

title: Upset customer
public_brief: Arjun is an existing customer and called in angry about a problem. Calm things down and agree a fix.

customer.name: Arjun
customer.persona: Runs two restaurants. Direct, loud when stressed, fair once he feels heard.
customer.situation: His month-end report did not match his bank and his accountant is waiting.
hidden_objections: Feels he was oversold when he signed up
customer.wins_if: The agent lets him finish, acknowledges the problem, explains honestly what happened, and agrees a concrete fix.
customer.walks_away_if: The agent blames him, gets defensive, or tries to sell him something before fixing the problem.

opening_line: I need someone to explain why my numbers are wrong. Again.

goals.name: Let him vent
goals.description: Acknowledge the frustration before explaining anything

goals.name: Explain honestly
goals.description: Say what happened without blame or overpromising

goals.name: Agree a fix
goals.description: End with a specific next step and when it will happen

title: Renewal and upsell
public_brief: Farah's yearly plan renews next week. She has hinted at cancelling. Keep her, and offer a better plan only if it fits.

customer.name: Farah
customer.persona: Finance manager at a 30-person trading company. Calm, numbers-driven, asks pointed questions.
customer.situation: Her CFO asked her to cut software costs by 15 percent this year.
hidden_objections: Thinks they only use half the features
A cheaper tool was suggested by a colleague
Doesn't want to look bad in front of the CFO
customer.wins_if: The agent asks how the team uses the product, works with her cost goal, and offers the right plan without pressure.
customer.walks_away_if: The agent dodges the price question or pushes a bigger plan she did not ask for.

opening_line: Hi. Before we talk renewal, I should tell you we're reviewing all our software spend.

goals.name: Understand usage
goals.description: Ask how her team uses the product today

goals.name: Handle the price concern
goals.description: Take the cost goal seriously and answer it directly

goals.name: Right-size the plan
goals.description: Offer the plan that fits her needs, bigger or smaller, without pressure

title: Support escalation
public_brief: Mr Iyer has raised three support tickets about the same issue and asked for a manager. Own the problem.

customer.name: Mr Iyer
customer.persona: Senior accountant who manages books for twelve small clients. Precise, formal, short on patience.
customer.situation: Bank feeds for two of his clients stopped syncing a week ago and each ticket got a different answer.
hidden_objections: Wants one named person who owns the issue
Is recommending a competitor to a new client this week
customer.wins_if: The agent apologises once, takes ownership, sets a realistic timeline, and confirms how and when he will hear back.
customer.walks_away_if: The agent reads out generic troubleshooting steps or promises a fix date they cannot back up.

opening_line: This is my third ticket. I'd like to speak to someone who can actually fix it.

goals.name: Own the problem
goals.description: Take personal ownership instead of passing it on

goals.name: Set expectations
goals.description: Give a realistic timeline without overpromising

goals.name: Confirm the next step
goals.description: Agree how and when he will hear back
